source.title: SCITT AI-Agent Action Receipts (individual draft, -00)
source.note: Read from the vendored copy in this repository, not from memory. The draft is an individual submission, not an adopted standard; nothing here claims that it is.

rows.note: Same role, different string. A reader that keys on "noa.receipt/0.1" will not find us.

rows.ours: no id field; the bytes are addressed by their sha256 in the lab bundle
rows.note: Addressable but not self-identifying: the digest lives in CORPUS-DIGESTS.txt, not in the receipt.
rows.cost: one field, plus a rule that it is the digest of the body

rows.note: Written by the runner at completion, second resolution, Z suffix.
We have no tenant and no per-issuer chain: a receipt belongs to whoever ran it.
rows.cost: requires an issuer identity and a chain head per tenant; without an operator this is a schema with no owner

rows.note: Free text, filled by the runner. The draft calls its own agent.id 'signer-asserted'; ours is runner-asserted and unsigned.

rows.ours: nothing (receipt.python and receipt.platform record the environment, not the model)
rows.note: Deliberately not faked: naming a model would be a claim about which system produced behaviour we do not observe.
rows.cost: nothing payable: the receipt side cannot observe the model, so the field would be filled by the runner and would carry the same authority as run_by, which is none

rows.note: Our receipts do not classify who acted; run_by is a string with no enum.
rows.cost: one enum plus a rule that an unfilled principal fails closed

rows.note: The action is a conformance case, identified by id and attack class; there is no risk class because a case is not a risky action.

rows.ours: receipt.manifest_sha256 (the corpus, not the action parameters)
rows.note: Structurally the same idea - bind by digest, keep raw material out - applied to a different object. Not a substitute.
rows.cost: the corpus digest exists; an action-parameter digest does not, because we have no action parameters

rows.note: Verification is side-effect free, so there is nothing to roll back.
rows.cost: nothing payable: adding the field would create a column with no values to fill it

rows.ours: rows[].verdict + rows[].reported (check names) + docs/DELEGATION.md for who was allowed
rows.note: Verdicts and rule names we have per case; an approval attached to a run we do not, except as a separate delegation record.

rows.theirs: chain.seq + chain.prevHash + chain.hash, hash over JCS(body without hash and without signature)
rows.ours: same construction, different object: tools/anchor_release_digests.py signs sha256 over the canonical body minus the signature; the change ledger chains by previous_id
rows.note: Our receipt stream is not chained - each receipt stands alone, linked only by the corpus digest it names. The chaining exists for the change ledger, not for receipts.
rows.cost: a seq and prev_hash per receipt, and a rule that a gap fails closed

rows.theirs: hash-chaining detects in-band tampering and tail truncation, NOT equivocation (needs transparency registration)
rows.ours: the same limit, stated in docs/LAB-PROTOCOL.md: a bundle proves the bytes cannot be changed after the fact, not that a run happened
rows.note: Both documents refuse to let chaining imply existence.

rows.theirs: registration in a SCITT Transparency Service
rows.ours: none; we anchor to an RFC 3161 TSA and, where a client exists, OpenTimestamps
rows.note: A timestamp proves the bytes existed at a time; it does not prove a log accepted them. We say this rather than call a TSA a transparency service.
rows.cost: an operator, a log, a registration policy, and the receipt container the log expects

rows.theirs: identity manifest binding agent.id to authorized kid(s); without one, attribution is key-level only and MUST be surfaced
rows.ours: docs/DELEGATION.md binds a name and an id to a key for one hop; the checker prints 'identity unbound' when the key is not supplied out of band
rows.note: The draft's own rule - surface the limitation - is the rule we implemented. Ours covers one hop and one operation; theirs covers an agent's whole key set.
rows.cost: a manifest listing keys per identity, and a rule that an unlisted pairing is UNTRUSTED

rows.theirs: COSE_Sign1 container, alg = -19 Ed25519 mandatory, other algs rejected
rows.ours: detached Ed25519 sidecar with alg fixed to "ed25519" and any other alg refused
rows.note: The rejection rule is the same; the container is not. No CBOR, no COSE, no interop.
rows.cost: a CBOR encoder and a COSE_Sign1 path; until then 'compatible' is the wrong word

rows.theirs: deterministic CBOR, non-canonical encodings rejected by the verifier
rows.ours: JCS canonicalisation on write; parsed JSON on read, so we never see a non-canonical encoding to reject
rows.note: We canonicalise what we produce; we cannot reject what we never parse as bytes.
rows.cost: receipts verified as bytes rather than as parsed objects

rows.theirs: policy-replay explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this revision
rows.ours: per-case replay is the product: 294 cases, three controls, an exit-code contract
rows.note: This is the one row where we do more: the draft defers replay to a later revision.
